name: Oxbit
subtitle: Code anywhere on iPhone & iPad
promotionalText: A real editor in your pocket. Edit local files, preview HTML and Markdown, and manage projects on iPhone and iPad.
description:
Oxbit brings a full code editor to iPhone and iPad. Open the Oxbit folder in Files or choose a project folder, then edit your source files on the device.

Write TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, JSON, and Markdown with syntax highlighting, search, formatting, and local language tools. Preview HTML and CSS together, or read rendered Markdown. Unsaved drafts and your workspace layout restore when you return.

Browse files, switch panels, and choose a theme that suits you. On iPad, split the editor to keep code and previews side by side. The keyboard accessory adds Tab, Escape, arrows, symbols, and undo and redo.

Connect an Oxbit runtime on your computer for its terminals, tasks, and additional language services. Local editing and previews work without a runtime.

Oxbit is free and open source. Requires iOS or iPadOS 26 or later.
whatsNew: Improved iPhone navigation and panel switching. HTML previews now leave more room for your page. Refined editor borders, breadcrumbs, and notification alignment. Fixed workspace switching, on-device language-server startup, and JSONC formatting.
reviewNotes: Local editing does not require an account. Open Oxbit under On this device, then create files using the Explorer controls. Open Folder uses the Files app picker. A computer runtime is optional and enables terminals and tasks for that computer's workspace.
